profile: release (opt-level s, LTO enabled; gpu-lines and pdf-content opt-level 3)

stages.after: Character erasing and PDFium fallback before the performance fixes
stages.optimized: Cached selection views, one traversal for all erasure regions, shared glyph outlines
stages.repeat: Three alternating before/optimized process pairs, with no concurrent builds

samples_per_process.selection: 21 batches: 20 uncached or 100 cached accesses per batch; milliseconds per access
samples_per_process.save: 7 saves, each reopening the unchanged source PDF before timing
samples_per_process.warmup: One discarded sample for each operation

fixtures.text-52000: 5 columns, each 130 rows of 80 Helvetica characters
fixtures.type3-4000: 50 rows of 80 characters in a PDF Type 3 font

scope: Synthetic pages; CPU renderer preparation, text extraction, selection filtering and real worker saves. Does not measure GPU drawing or interactive panning/zooming frame rates.
interpretation: Renderer preparation showed no slowdown in the alternating runs. Initial text extraction remains about 10% more expensive and characters use more cache memory because ink bounds are retained. Cached selection avoids repeated filtering; the filter is rebuilt after erasure changes or text reloads. Correct character removal still costs more than the previous visual-only clipping when saving.
commands: Run each compiled test executable with --ignored --nocapture and ERASE_BENCH_LABEL set
